Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley (author, Wikidata Q47152), died 1851; Percy Bysshe Shelley (author, Wikidata Q93343), died 1822. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Shelley, Mary Wollstonecraft, 1797-1851; Shelley, Percy Bysshe, 1792-1822") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: History of a six weeks' tour through a part of France, Switzerland, Germany and Holland: with letters descriptive of a sail round the Lake of Geneva, and of the glaciers of Chamouni, London : Published by T. Hookham, jun. Old Bond Street; and C. and J. Ollier, Welbeck street, 1817, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/sixweekhistoryof00shelrich. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 100%, 86%, 85% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley, Percy Bysshe Shelley, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
